pr_title: py/nlr: Factor out common NLR code to generic functions.
pr_body:
Each NLR implementation (Thumb, x86, x64, xtensa, setjmp) duplicates a lot
of the NLR code, specifically that dealing with pushing and popping the NLR
pointer to maintain the linked-list of NLR buffers.  This patch factors all
of that code out of the specific implementations into generic functions in
nlr.c.  This eliminates duplicated code.

The factoring also allows to make the machine-specific NLR code pure
assembler code, thus allowing nlrthumb.c to use naked function attributes
in the correct way (naked functions can only have basic inline assembler
code in them).

There is a small overhead introduced (typically 1 machine instruction)
because now the generic nlr_jump() must call nlr_jump_tail() rather than
them being one combined function.

Should fix #3484

issue_context.title: naked attribute on nlr_push - Only basic asm statements can safely be included in naked functions
issue_context.body:
One example:

https://github.com/micropython/micropython/blob/d3f82bc42576ccd80206a17a4941fd5c28c56530/py/nlrthumb.c#L70-L81

naked
[This attribute allows the compiler to construct the requisite function declaration, while allowing the body of the function to be assembly code. The specified function will not have prologue/epilogue sequences generated by the compiler. Only basic asm statements can safely be included in naked functions (see Basic Asm). While using extended asm or a mixture of basic asm and C code may appear to work, they cannot be depended upon to work reliably and are not supported.](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/ARM-Function-Attributes.html#ARM-Function-Attributes)

`return 0` must be removed from all `naked nlr_push` functions.
comments:
> return 0 must be removed from all naked nlr_push functions.

As mentioned in the code, it's only there to silence compiler warnings.

@adritium: Thanks for opening this issue. I meant to do this myself, but other things took precedence.

As things stand now, micropython and clang do not go together.

> it's causing the compilation to FAIL on clang

Using clang 5.0.0 on an x86-64 arch I don't see any issues compiling py/nlrx64.c, but I guess it could be a problem with other clang versions on other archs.

> If negating a gcc compiler warning causes a clang compiler failure, I don't think the trade-off is correct,

It's not a trade off, both things should be properly fixed.  Is there a suggestion how to fix it?

>  but I guess it could be a problem with other clang versions on other archs.

Yes, I encountered this on armv7 (Samsung Galaxy S5 mini and Raspberry Pi 3). Arm64 worked fine.

> What is the warning?
> 
> Maybe there's a bug in the gcc warning code?

I agree it's inconsistent for gcc to say only use basic asm in naked functions, and then give a warning about not returning a value.  Revisiting the code now, removing the return statement from the naked nlr_push() function doesn't induce a warning.  So either a newer version of gcc fixed the issue, or the return was added incorrectly (maybe before the function became naked).

Anyway, I've attempted to fix it all properly in #3492, and in doing so take the chance to factor all the common NLR code into one place to clean up the individual machine-specific implementations.  Please take a look at that PR to see if it solves the issue.

review_comments: @stinos furthermore: for `__CYGWIN__` why is it 12 regs and not 10 (an extra 2 for rsi and rdi compared with non-unix)?  And why isn't this check `defined(_WIN32) || defined(__CYGWIN__)` to match the definition of the `NLR_OS_WINDOWS` macro?

Not sure. This was introduced years ago by you and it didn't change since. However I think this might actually have been an oversight in #1632 and follow up bf1570cb2559ba12ca86b2dbb26be665300ffe5e: there the _WIN32 got introduced but nlr.h has not been changed. And this seems very wrong (not tested, but in nlrx64 I see more movq calls than there is space in nlr->regs, right?) So that might even be the reason why 64bit msys mingw builds segfault (assuming they still do). Not sure what the best way to solve this would be now: I don't have time to test all of this right now, though I do next week. So either you leave it as-is and we'll see later one, or you do something like declaring NLR_OS_WINDOWS in nlr.h so it can be used both there to enable set MICROPY_NLR_NUM_REGS to 12 and in nlr.c?

> This was introduced years ago by you and it didn't change since

Indeed!  And it looks like it allocates 2 more slots than it needs to.

> there the _WIN32 got introduced but nlr.h has not been changed. And this seems very wrong (not tested, but in nlrx64 I see more movq calls than there is space in nlr->regs, right?)

Yes it seems wrong.

Ok, let's leave this particular issue until later.  For now I've aimed to make this PR not change any behaviour, as far as that is possible.
